extracted.intended_audience: graduate students / researchers in algebraic geometry (Math 216 level)
extracted.subtask_description: Statements, criteria, and technical lemmas governing how sheaf cohomology behaves in families: semicontinuity, Grauert's theorem, the Cohomology-and-Base-Change theorem, descent of line bundles, and the linear-algebraic reduction (Mumford’s key theorem).

rubrics_metrics.name: Property (a): fiberwise base-change isomorphism φ^p_q
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a fibered square (28.1.0.1), the natural map φ^p_q : (R^p π_* F) ⊗ κ(q) → H^p(X_q, F|_{X_q}) — is it an isomorphism?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one of the three central properties to check for a proper flat family with coherent F; semicontinuity controls the dimensions appearing on the right-hand side and is a first step toward understanding when φ^p_q is an iso. See Cohomology and Base Change Theorem 28.1.6 for precise sufficient conditions (surjectivity at q implies local isomorphism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Property (b): base-change for pullbacks φ^p_Z
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a fibered square (28.1.0.2), is the natural map φ^p_Z: ψ^*(R^p π_* F) → R^p π'_*(ψ')^*F an isomorphism?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statement that R^p π_* F commutes with arbitrary base change. Grauert’s theorem and the Cohomology-and-Base-Change theorem give hypotheses guaranteeing this (e.g., local freeness of R^p π_* F, surjectivity of the stalk map, or flat base change).

rubrics_metrics.name: Property (c): local freeness of R^p π_* F
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the sheaf R^p π_* F locally free (a vector bundle) on Y?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local freeness of R^p π_* F is intimately tied to base-change isomorphisms: if R^p π_* F is locally free then fibers identify with cohomology of the fiber; conversely, constancy of h^p often implies local freeness (Grauert). Cohomology-and-Base-Change gives precise equivalences involving surjectivity of φ^p_q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semicontinuity Theorem (28.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π: X → Y is proper, Y Noetherian, and F is coherent and flat over Y. Then for each p the function q ↦ dim_{κ(q)} H^p(X_q, F|_{X_q}) is upper semicontinuous on Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation: cohomology dimensions of fibers cannot increase on small neighborhoods; jumps occur only on closed loci. Proof reduces to linear algebra on a complex of finite free modules (Key Theorem 28.2.1) and the fact that ranks of matrices drop on closed subsets (vanishing of minors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grauert’s Theorem (28.1.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is proper, Y reduced and locally Noetherian, F coherent flat over Y, and h^p(X_q, F|_{X_q}) is locally constant in q, then R^p π_* F is locally free and φ^p_Z is an isomorphism for all ψ: Z → Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial converse to (a): constancy of fiber dimension (over a reduced base) allows gluing into a vector bundle and identifies fibers with cohomology. No Noetherian hypothesis is needed in the version stated here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology and Base Change Theorem (28.1.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π is proper, Y locally Noetherian, F coherent and flat over Y, and the stalk map φ^p_q is surjective. Then (i) there exists a neighborhood U of q such that for any ψ: Z → U the base-change map φ^p_Z is an isomorphism; (ii) φ^{p-1}_q is an isomorphism. Moreover, φ^p_q is surjective iff R^p π_* F is free in a neighborhood of q (equivalently (R^p π_* F)_q free), which implies constancy of h^p nearby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This theorem gives a local criterion (surjectivity at a point) that forces base-change isomorphisms in a neighborhood and relates these to local freeness. The surprising feature: a condition checked on reduced points controls behavior on possible nilpotents as well (using local flatness criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat base change (reference to Theorem 24.2.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohomology commutes with flat base change: if ψ is flat then the natural base-change maps are isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a common sufficient hypothesis: flat pullbacks preserve the formation of pushforwards and cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euler characteristic constancy (Theorem 24.7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is flat over Y and π proper, then the Euler characteristic χ(X_q, F|_{X_q}) is locally constant in families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a weaker invariant than individual h^p; Grauert-type arguments and the finite free complex J• construction show χ is locally constant by expressing it as an alternating sum of ranks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking constancy on closed points for quasicompact Y
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y is quasicompact then by semicontinuity it suffices to check that h^p(X_q, F|_{X_q}) is constant at closed points to deduce constancy on Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces global checking to a (often manageable) finite set of closed points; relies on the Semicontinuity Theorem and properties of Noetherian/quasicompact schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic/local openness of locus where R^p π_* F is locally free
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y is integral, π proper, and F coherent flat over Y, there is a dense open subset of Y on which R^p π_* F is locally free and fibers identify with cohomology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semicontinuity implies that fiber-dimensions are constant on a dense open, which by Grauert yields local freeness on that open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper O-connected morphisms and criterion (Definition / 28.1.7 & 28.1.H)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism π: X → Y is O-connected if the natural map O_Y → π_* O_X is an isomorphism. For a proper flat morphism whose fibers satisfy h^0(X_q, O_{X_q}) = 1, π is O-connected (hence π_* O_X ≅ O_Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: O-connectedness captures the right notion of 'connected fibers' in many contexts; exercise shows it follows from geometric connectedness + reducedness and is stable under flat base change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descent of invertible sheaves (Proposition 28.1.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is flat, proper, O-connected, locally Noetherian, Y reduced, and L is an invertible sheaf on X trivial on every fiber, then π_* L is invertible on Y and the natural map π^* π_* L → L is an isomorphism (i.e., L is pulled back from Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a practical criterion to decide when a line bundle on X descends from the base: check fiberwise triviality, O-connectedness, and the reduced hypothesis (which can be removed using Cohomology-and-Base-Change).

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective bundle criterion (Exercises 28.1.J and 28.1.L)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is a projective flat morphism whose geometric fibers are isomorphic to P^n, then π is a P^n-bundle iff there exists an invertible sheaf on X restricting to O(1) on every fiber. Equivalently, π_* O(1) should be a locally free sheaf whose projectivization recovers X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One direction is obvious; the other uses Cohomology-and-Base-Change to show π_* O(1) is locally free of the right rank and that Proj Sym^•(π_* O(1)) reconstructs X. Beware counterexamples when finite presentation/other hypotheses fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picard / Picard-scheme remarks (28.1.K / 28.1.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements that Pic(X) 'wants to be a scheme' and in special cases (e.g., P^n-bundles) Pic can be described explicitly (Pic P^n_Z ≅ Pic Z ⊕ Z).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are guidelines for assessing when families of line bundles form representable functors; constructing the Picard scheme typically uses cohomology-and-base-change technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hodge bundle construction (28.1.N)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is flat proper with fibers regular irreducible curves of genus g, then π_* Ω_{X/Y} is locally free of rank g (the Hodge bundle) and formation commutes with base change: Ω_{X'/Y'} ≅ (ψ')^* Ω_{X/Y}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This uses Cohomology-and-Base-Change applied to p = 1 and p = 2; provides a canonical vector bundle of rank g on the base parameterizing differentials in families of smooth curves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Theorem (Mumford) 28.2.1: finite free complex model
rubrics_metrics.description: For π: X → Spec B proper and F coherent flat over Spec B, there exists a (possibly infinite to the left) complex K• of finitely generated free B-modules and functorial isomorphisms Hp(X ×_B Spec A, F ⊗_B A) ≅ Hp(K• ⊗_B A) for every B-algebra A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central reduction: questions about R^p π_* F and base change reduce to linear algebra of matrices with entries in B (the differentials of K•). It underlies semicontinuity and Grauert/Cohomology-and-Base-Change proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 28.2.2: exist finite-rank free complex quasi-isomorphic to coherent complex
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a bounded-above complex C• with coherent (finitely generated) cohomology over a Noetherian ring B, there exists a complex K• of finite rank free B-modules quasi-isomorphic to C• (isomorphism on cohomology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructed inductively by choosing lifts of cohomology generators; a key step in producing the finite free model K• used in Key Theorem 28.2.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 28.2.3: quasi-isomorphisms commute with arbitrary base change
rubrics_metrics.description: If α: K• → C• is a quasi-isomorphism between complexes of flat B-modules, then for every B-algebra A the induced maps on cohomology Hp(K• ⊗_B A) → Hp(C• ⊗_B A) are isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to show the finite free model K• computes cohomology after any base change; proof via mapping cone exactness and base-change properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic criterion for semicontinuity via minors / ranks of matrices
rubrics_metrics.description: When cohomology is computed by a finite free complex K•, dim H^p(X_q,F|_{X_q}) can be written in terms of dimensions of kernels and images of differentials δ_p ⊗ κ(q); the locus where these dimensions drop is cut out by vanishing of minors of the matrices representing δ_p, hence closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the explicit linear-algebraic mechanism behind upper semicontinuity: ranks of matrices are lower-semicontinuous functions, so kernels/dimensions are upper-semicontinuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness/vanishing criteria in the K•-language (Exercises 28.2.E–28.2.K)
rubrics_metrics.description: If W_p K• and W_{p+1} K• (cokernels of differentials) are flat (locally free), then base-change (b) and hence (a) holds; R^p π_* F is locally free under reduced or locally Noetherian hypotheses. Moreover, surjectivity of φ^p_q forces flatness of certain W's and hence local freeness of H^p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exercises give the chain of implications used to prove Grauert and Cohomology-and-Base-Change: check flatness of cokernels / images in the finite-free complex model, translate to vanishing of R^1 functors via the local criterion for flatness, and conclude local freeness and base-change properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of finite-presentation hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Finite-presentation (or Noetherian-type) hypotheses are necessary: there exist projective flat morphisms to a connected target where fiber-dimension or arithmetic genus jumps if finite-presentation is dropped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning/anti-pattern: without finite-presentation (or analogous hypotheses) the pleasant behaviors (constancy, local freeness, base-change) can fail; the text references explicit counterexamples and Stacks project tags.
